claim_verdicts.evidence: OrdersController.cs @stage-1: `Create`'s body has no `if`/`switch`; the only `return` is `return CreatedAtAction(nameof(Get), new { id = order.Id }, ToDto(order));`. The lines before it only read `customerId`, build `items`, and await `PlaceOrderAsync`. The quoted block (lines 9-28) matches `tools/extract-code ... --tag stage-1 --lines 9-28` character for character.

RFC 9110 §9.3.3, verbatim in the local mirror: "If one or more resources has been created on the origin server as a result of successfully processing a POST request, the origin server SHOULD send a 201 (Created) response containing a Location header field that provides an identifier for the primary resource created (Section 10.2.2) and a representation that describes the status of the request while referring to the new resource(s)."

claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 9110 §9.2.2, verbatim: "A request method is considered 'idempotent' if the intended effect on the server of multiple identical requests with that method is the same as the effect for a single such request. Of the request methods defined by this specification, PUT, DELETE, and safe request methods are idempotent." POST is absent from that list. Same section: repeating an idempotent request has "the same intended effect ... though the response might differ".

Dtos.cs @stage-1: `public sealed record CreateOrderRequest(List<CreateOrderItemRequest> Items);` — one positional parameter, no id. `CreateOrderItemRequest(int ProductId, int Quantity, int UnitPriceVnd)` has no id either, so no id can be sent at any level of the body.

ASP.NET Core docs: "A 201 status code is generated by the CreatedAtAction method when a product is created. In this code path, the Product object is provided in the response body. A `Location` response header containing the newly created product's URL is provided." Route source confirmed by execution: `OrdersController.Get` is `[HttpGet("{id:int}")]` under `[Route("api/v1/orders")]`, and a live POST answered `Location: http://localhost:8080/api/v1/orders/17`.
claim_verdicts.source: refs/aspnetcore-docs/aspnetcore/web-api/action-return-types.md line 143; live run 2026-09-24 against stage-1 lab

issues.text: Idempotence is stated as "the response is the same", which is not what it means and is not what the next lesson will teach. RFC 9110 §9.2.2 defines it as "the intended effect on the server of multiple identical requests ... is the same as the effect for a single such request" and adds that repeating an idempotent request has the same effect "though the response might differ". A second `GET` can legitimately return different bytes; what it cannot do is change the server. Section 4 repeats it: "Repeating the exact same `POST` doesn't repeat the exact same result the way repeating a `GET` does."
issues.quote: unlike a `GET`, which just re-reads the same thing every time
issues.fix: Core concepts: "— unlike a `GET`, which leaves the server exactly as it was however many times it is sent." How it works, first sentence of the third paragraph: "Repeating the exact same `POST` changes the server again each time; repeating a `GET` never does." Keep the rest of that paragraph unchanged — "Each successful `Create` call makes one more row" is already the correct framing.

issues.text: The `fill` answer set has a single spelling, `["Location"]`. HTTP field names are case-insensitive (RFC 9110 §5.1: "Field names are case-insensitive"), so a learner typing `location` gives a correct answer and is marked wrong. Sibling lessons in this module do list every accepted spelling — get-and-status-codes q3 is `["NotFound", "NotFound()", "return NotFound"]`, dtos-and-serialization q3 is `["priceVnd", "\"priceVnd\""]`.

issues.text: `[Authorize]` does not read the `Authorization` header. In Program.cs @stage-1 the JWT bearer handler (`AddAuthentication(JwtBearerDefaults.AuthenticationScheme).AddJwtBearer(...)`, run by `app.UseAuthentication()`) parses the header and builds the principal; `[Authorize]` then checks whether that principal is authenticated. Docs: `[Authorize]` "limits access to that component to authenticated users" — it is a check on identity, not on a header.
issues.quote: step 2 sends it back in the `Authorization` header, which is what `[Authorize]` checks
issues.fix: Write: "step 2 sends it back in the `Authorization` header, which is how the server knows who is calling before `[Authorize]` lets the request through."

issues.text: "none of which create a new resource" is too strong for `PUT`. RFC 9110 §9.3.4: "If the target resource does not have a current representation and the PUT successfully creates one, then the origin server MUST inform the user agent by sending a 201 (Created) response." The trailing hedge "the way `POST` does here" carries the whole sentence, and a reader who drops it leaves with "PUT never creates" right before the lesson that teaches PUT.
issues.quote: none of which create a new resource the way `POST` does here
issues.fix: Write: "— the remaining write methods, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, none of which have the server choose a brand-new URL the way `POST` does here."

issues.text: Option c is a fair distractor (it describes `202`, so it is correctly marked wrong for a question about `201`), but its explanation is false as HTTP: "An in-progress request has no final status code yet at all." RFC 9110 §15.3.3: "The 202 (Accepted) status code indicates that the request has been accepted for processing, but the processing has not been completed." A server does answer with a final code while work continues.
issues.quote: An in-progress request has no final status code yet at all; `201` is a completed answer, not a placeholder for one still running.
issues.fix: Rewrite c's explanation without asserting anything about in-progress requests: "`201` is the answer to a request that has already finished creating something — it never means the work is still running. Nothing in this lesson's `Create` answers before the row exists." Mirror the same wording in the `vi` explanation.
